blockMcqs.question: Which traversal gives the shortest path in an unweighted graph?
options: DFS, because it goes deep fast
BFS, because it explores level by level
Either one, results are identical
Neither without edge weights
blockMcqs.explanation: Ring-by-ring order means the first arrival uses the fewest edges.

blockMcqs.question: Why is an adjacency list preferred for most real graphs?
options: It answers "is u→v an edge?" in O(1)
Real graphs are sparse, so O(V+E) space wins
It supports weighted edges and matrices don't
It keeps neighbors in sorted order
blockMcqs.explanation: A matrix wastes O(V²) memory when edges are far fewer than V².

blockMcqs.question: Storing an undirected edge in only one neighbor list causes what?
options: A duplicate edge counted twice
An O(V²) blow-up in memory
Traversal treats the graph as directed
A guaranteed cycle on every run
blockMcqs.explanation: Only one direction exists, so some reachable vertices are silently missed.

blockMcqs.question: When should BFS mark a vertex as visited?
options: When it is dequeued and processed
When it is enqueued
After all its neighbors finish
Only once at the very end
blockMcqs.explanation: Marking at dequeue lets several neighbors enqueue the same vertex first.

blockMcqs.question: In recursive DFS, what runs in post-order?
options: Work done when a vertex is first seen
Work done after all descendants finish
Work done only at the source vertex
Work done for every edge twice
blockMcqs.explanation: Pre-order acts on first sight; post-order is the moment of return.

blockMcqs.question: How does directed-graph DFS detect a cycle?
options: It revisits any already-visited vertex
It reaches a vertex that is not its parent
It reaches a gray vertex on the current path
It finishes with fewer than V vertices
blockMcqs.explanation: An edge to a finished black vertex is fine; only a back edge means a cycle.

blockMcqs.question: In Kahn's algorithm, what does an output shorter than V mean?
options: The graph is disconnected
The graph contains a cycle
The start vertex was wrong
The graph is undirected
blockMcqs.explanation: Vertices stuck in a cycle never reach in-degree zero to be emitted.

blockMcqs.question: On a very wide graph, why can BFS use more memory than DFS?
options: BFS stores the full adjacency matrix
Its queue can hold an entire level at once
It revisits vertices it already marked
It recurses deeper than DFS does
blockMcqs.explanation: DFS memory tracks depth, while BFS memory tracks a level's width.

blockMcqs.question: A spreadsheet's "circular reference" error is really which check?
options: A load-factor threshold being crossed
Cycle detection on the cell dependency DAG
A failed topological sort of all sheets
An out-of-memory guard on the queue
blockMcqs.explanation: Cells depend on cells; a self-referential formula forms a cycle with no valid recompute order.

blockMcqs.question: Which claim about graph traversal is actually false?
options: DFS guarantees the shortest unweighted path
Undirected cycle detection skips the parent
Topological sort requires a DAG
BFS should mark visited at enqueue time
blockMcqs.explanation: DFS finds some path; only BFS or Dijkstra guarantee the shortest.
